heroIntro: Picture a nightmare scenario: you negotiate the purchase of a valuable plot of land in Dhaka, pay the agreed consideration, execute and register a formal Saf Kabala deed at the Sub-Registry Office, and begin preparing for mutation. Months later, you arrive at the property only to find construction materials piled high and an aggressive stranger waving a deed, claiming they purchased the exact same plot from your seller. In Bangladesh's heated real estate market, 'double sale' (selling the same land to multiple buyers) is one of the most destructive forms of property swindling. Fortunately, under the Registration Act 1908, the Specific Relief Act 1877, and the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023, the law strictly protects the prior registered purchaser and prescribes severe criminal punishment—including up to 7 years non-bailable imprisonment—for fraudulent sellers.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer: What Can You Do If a Seller Sells Your Land to a Second Buyer in Bangladesh?
quickAnswer.text: Under Section 48 and Section 49 of the Registration Act 1908, an earlier registered deed takes absolute priority over any subsequent deed. Once a seller executes and registers a valid Saf Kabala deed in your favor, they lose all ownership and title; any subsequent transfer to a second buyer is void ab initio (invalid from the start). To secure your property, you must immediately file a Title Suit in the Civil Court under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 for Cancellation of the Subsequent Deed and Section 42 for Declaration of Title, accompanied by an urgent petition under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) for a Temporary Injunction restraining any construction or third-party sale. Furthermore, under Section 4 and Section 5 of the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023, you can file a criminal case against the fraudulent seller, who faces up to 7 years non-bailable rigorous imprisonment.
highlights: The earlier registered deed takes absolute priority in law; the seller had no remaining title to convey to a second buyer.
Under the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023, executing a double sale carries up to 7 years non-bailable imprisonment.
Civil remedies require filing a Title Suit under Specific Relief Act §39 to cancel the second fraudulent deed.
An immediate Temporary Injunction (Order 39 CPC) prevents the second buyer from altering possession or building structures.
points: Step 1: Obtain certified copies of both your deed and the fraudulent subsequent deed from the Sub-Registry Office (Balam search).
Step 2: File an urgent Title Suit for Declaration of Title and Cancellation of the second deed under Specific Relief Act §§39 & 42.
Step 3: Secure an immediate ex parte Temporary Injunction (Order 39 CPC) restraining all construction and further transfers.
Step 4: Institute criminal proceedings under Land Crime Act 2023 and Penal Code §420 to arrest the fraudulent seller.

sections.title: The Anatomy of Double Sale Land Fraud in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Land in Bangladesh is exceptionally scarce and commands astronomical market valuations, particularly across Dhaka, Chattogram, and rapidly urbanizing district headquarters. This scarcity has fueled predatory land syndicates and unscrupulous sellers who exploit administrative backlogs between the Sub-Registry Office and the Assistant Commissioner (Land) office. In a typical double sale scheme, a landowner sells a plot to Buyer A, receives the full purchase price, and executes a registered Saf Kabala deed. However, before Buyer A completes their field mutation (Namjari) and updates the revenue records, the dishonest seller takes advantage of the fact that the old RS or BS Khatian still displays their name, and executes a second registered deed for the same plot to Buyer B, pocketing money twice.

In other scenarios, sellers execute an unregistered Bayna deed (agreement for sale) with Buyer A, take a heavy advance, and then secretly sell the property outright to Buyer B. Regardless of the exact variation, discovering that your purchased land has been transferred to another person causes overwhelming panic. Understanding how property registration statutes and landmark 2023 criminal enactments operate is crucial to reclaiming your rightful property.

sections.title: Priority of Deeds Under the Registration Act 1908
sections.content:
The foundational bedrock of Bangladesh property law is the doctrine of priority. Under Section 47 of the Registration Act 1908, a registered document operates not from the date of its ultimate delivery from the registry office, but from the time from which it would have commenced to operate whether no registration thereof had been required—meaning from the date of its original execution.

Furthermore, under Section 48 and Section 49 of the Registration Act 1908, a registered document relating to land takes absolute effect against any subsequent or unrecorded claim. Under the Latin maxim Nemo dat quod non habet (no one can give what they do not have), once the seller executed and registered the first Saf Kabala deed in favor of Buyer A, the seller's entire right, title, and interest were completely extinguished. The seller possessed zero title to transfer to Buyer B. Consequently, the second deed is a legal nullity (void ab initio), conveying nothing to the second buyer regardless of how much money they paid.

sections.title: Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023: Heavy Penalties
sections.content:
Historically, victims of double sale fraud were forced to endure decades of sluggish civil litigation while fraudulent sellers enjoyed their illicit millions. To terminate this culture of impunity, the Parliament of Bangladesh enacted the historic Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023 (Bhumi Oporadh Protirodh O Protikar Ain 2023).

This landmark statute specifically criminalizes fraudulent double transactions:

  • Section 4 (Fraudulent Document Execution): Creating, signing, or registering any deed or document knowing that the seller does not possess lawful ownership or has already alienated the property is a cognizable and non-bailable offense.
  • Section 5 (Selling Land Multiple Times): Executing a deed of sale or transfer for land that has already been sold or committed to another person carries rigorous imprisonment for up to seven (7) years and heavy monetary fines.
  • Summary Restitution Powers: The Act empowers Executive Magistrates and specialized courts to take immediate cognizance, issue non-bailable arrest warrants against fraudulent sellers, and issue summary possession protection orders.

Coupled with traditional charges under Section 420 (cheating) and Section 406 (criminal breach of trust) of the Penal Code 1860, this modern enactment gives defrauded buyers immediate, aggressive leverage against dishonest sellers.

sections.title: Civil Court Remedies: Deed Cancellation and Declaration
sections.content:
While criminal proceedings penalize the perpetrator, they do not automatically cancel the fraudulent second deed recorded in the Sub-Registry Office's volume books. To eliminate any cloud on your title, you must file a formal Title Suit in the Court of the Joint District Judge having territorial jurisdiction:

  1. Cancellation of Subsequent Deed (Section 39 Specific Relief Act 1877): Under Section 39, any person against whom a written instrument is void or voidable, and who has reasonable apprehension that such instrument, if left outstanding, may cause serious injury, may sue to have it adjudged void or cancelled. The court passes a decree directing the Sub-Registrar to record a note of cancellation against the fraudulent deed in the register.
  2. Declaration of Title (Section 42 Specific Relief Act 1877): The suit simultaneously seeks a judicial declaration that the plaintiff is the sole, exclusive, and rightful owner of the suit land by virtue of their prior registered deed.
  3. Permanent Injunction (Section 54 Specific Relief Act 1877): A perpetual injunction permanently restraining the defendant seller and the second purchaser from entering upon, disturbing possession of, or alienating the suit property.

Faced with a fraudulent land sale, double deed, or boundary grab in Bangladesh? Send your deeds and Khatian records on WhatsApp to +880 1955-802007. Overseas clients and local landowners can arrange an immediate title audit.

sections.title: Securing an Immediate Temporary Injunction (Order 39 CPC)
sections.content:
The single most urgent procedural step upon filing your Title Suit is moving an interlocutory application for a Temporary Injunction under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). If the second buyer begins pouring concrete, constructing boundary walls, or selling sub-plots to third parties, reversing that physical reality during a multi-year trial becomes an uphill battle.

To secure an injunction, your advocate must establish the three classic legal tests:

  • Prima Facie Case: Proved conclusively by presenting your certified earlier registered deed and payment receipts.
  • Balance of Convenience: Demonstrating that preserving the property in status quo favors the lawful prior purchaser rather than a fraudulent subsequent interloper.
  • Irreparable Injury: Proving that if the second buyer alters the topography or builds structures, monetary compensation will not adequately remedy the injury.

Upon satisfaction, the civil court grants an ad-interim injunction restraining both defendants from altering the physical character of the land, felling trees, raising structures, or executing further transfers until the disposal of the suit.

sections.title: Sub-Registry Office Balam Book Searches and Document Audits
sections.content:
To build an ironclad case, your advocate must conduct a forensic document audit at the relevant Sub-Registry Office. Many victims make the mistake of relying only on the paper deed handed to them. A comprehensive legal audit requires:

  1. Balam Book Search (Form 36): Conducting an official search in the Balam (volume) books and Index I/II for the past 12 to 25 years to trace every transaction executed under the relevant CS, SA, RS, and City/BS Khatian and Dag (plot) numbers.
  2. Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC): Applying for an official Non-Encumbrance Certificate from the Sub-Registrar confirming whether any mortgages, attachments, or secondary deeds have been recorded against the plot.
  3. Certified Copies of the Subsequent Deed: Procuring the certified copy of the second deed to inspect how the seller described their title, whether they forged an NID, or whether the second buyer acted in collusion with full knowledge of your prior purchase.

These certified extracts constitute primary documentary evidence that refutes any claim by the second buyer that they were an 'innocent purchaser without notice.'

sections.title: Role of AC Land Mutation and Kharij Contests
sections.content:
Parallel to the civil court battle, the administrative dispute plays out before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) office. If the second buyer has submitted an online mutation application (E-Namjari) to open a new Khatian in their name, you must immediately file a formal written objection.

Under the Land Management Manual and Ministry of Land circulars, an AC Land is strictly prohibited from mutating land in favor of a subsequent buyer when a prior registered deed exists for the exact same Dag and parcel. You must submit your certified prior deed, tax receipts (Dakhila), and a certified copy of the civil court's injunction order. The AC Land will reject the second buyer's mutation application (Namonjur), preventing them from acquiring revenue legitimacy. If the AC Land has already erroneously opened a Khatian for the second buyer, your advocate can file an E-Namjari Miss Case or an appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) under Section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 to cancel the fraudulent Khatian.

sections.title: Comparison Table: First Buyer Rights vs. Second Buyer
sections.content:
The table below outlines the legal status and rights of the competing purchasers in a double sale fraud scenario:

ParameterFirst Purchaser (Your Position)Second Purchaser (Subsequent Deed)
Legal Ownership & TitleAbsolute title under Registration Act §48Zero title; deed is void ab initio
Remedy Against DeedEntitled to decree of cancellation under §39Deed subject to mandatory court cancellation
Protection of PossessionProtected via Order 39 Injunction & §145Can be summarily evicted as illegal trespasser
Mutation (Namjari) RightLawfully entitled to Namjari KhatianMutation must be rejected / cancelled
Recourse for Stolen MoneyKeeps the land; can claim damagesMust sue seller for money refund under §420

As the first purchaser, the law stands entirely on your side. The second buyer's only lawful recourse is suing the fraudulent seller to recover their money.

sections.title: Illustrative Scenario: Defeating a Double Sale Syndicate
sections.content:
The following illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed) illustrates how aggressive civil and criminal actions dismantled a double sale fraud in Savar:

An expatriate living in Birmingham, UK, purchased a 5-katha residential plot in Savar in January 2024 for BDT 45,00,000. The seller executed and registered a valid Saf Kabala deed before the Savar Sub-Registrar. Because the buyer returned to the UK shortly after, he delayed physical possession and mutation. Eight months later, the seller, realizing the owner was abroad, executed a second registered deed for the exact same plot to a local housing company for BDT 55,00,000. When the expatriate's brother visited the plot in October 2024, the housing company had erected signboards and stationed private security guards.

Acting through a Special Power of Attorney, the expatriate engaged a Supreme Court advocate. The legal team immediately executed a three-pronged counter-attack: first, they filed a Title Suit in the Court of the Joint District Judge, Dhaka, for cancellation of the housing company's deed and declaration of title, successfully securing an ad-interim Temporary Injunction under Order 39 CPC halting all construction. Second, they filed a formal objection before the Savar AC Land, blocking the housing company's mutation application.

Third, the advocate lodged a criminal prosecution under Section 5 of the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023 and Section 420 of the Penal Code. The Magistrate Court issued non-bailable arrest warrants against the seller. Within forty-eight hours of the seller's arrest by police, the housing company, realizing their deed was legally worthless and facing injunction contempt proceedings, withdrew their guards. The seller's family was forced to refund the housing company's money to secure bail, and the expatriate's lawful ownership and mutation were fully restored.

sections.title: Talk to an Advocate
sections.content:
If you have discovered that a seller has fraudulently transferred your land to another buyer, time is your greatest adversary. Every day of delay allows the fraudulent party to erect structures, alter boundary demarcations, or sell to innocent third parties. A skilled land lawyer will immediately initiate Title Suit proceedings for deed cancellation, secure emergency injunctions from the civil court, block fraudulent mutations at the AC Land office, and invoke the stringent penal provisions of the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023.

faqs.question: Which buyer owns the land if a seller sells it twice in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The first buyer who executed and registered the valid Saf Kabala deed owns the land. Under Section 48 of the Registration Act 1908, prior registration takes absolute priority. Once the first deed is registered, the seller has no remaining title to pass to a second buyer.

faqs.question: What is the punishment for a seller who executes a double sale in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 5 of the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023, selling land to multiple parties carries rigorous imprisonment for up to 7 years and heavy fines. The offense is cognizable and non-bailable.

faqs.question: How do I cancel the second buyer's fraudulent deed?
faqs.answer: You must file a Title Suit in the Court of the Joint District Judge under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 for Cancellation of Deed. The court passes a decree adjudging the second deed void and directs the Sub-Registrar to record its cancellation.

faqs.question: Can the second buyer claim they are an innocent purchaser without notice?
faqs.answer: In real property law, registration in the official Sub-Registry Office Balam books operates as constructive notice to the entire world. A second buyer cannot claim innocence to defeat a valid, prior registered deed.

faqs.question: How can I prevent the second buyer from building on the land while the case is ongoing?
faqs.answer: Your advocate will file an application for a Temporary Injunction under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). The court can issue an immediate order restraining the second buyer from altering the land, felling trees, or building structures.

faqs.question: What if the second buyer already managed to get Namjari (mutation) in their name?
faqs.answer: You can file an E-Namjari Miss Case or an appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) under Section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. Since mutation does not create title, the revenue authority will cancel the Khatian upon presentation of the prior registered deed.

faqs.question: What happens if I only had an unregistered Bayna deed and the seller sold to someone else?
faqs.answer: Under Section 21A of the Specific Relief Act 1877, a contract for sale (Bayna) must be registered. If your Bayna deed was registered, you can sue for Specific Performance. If it was unregistered, you cannot compel transfer of the land and can only sue to recover your advance money with damages under the Penal Code.

faqs.question: Can an overseas Bangladeshi (NRB) pursue this litigation without coming to Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. An NRB landowner can execute a Special Power of Attorney attested by the Bangladesh High Commission or Embassy abroad, appointing a trusted local representative and retaining an advocate to handle the civil litigation and police complaints.
